section: National Commission for SCs (338), STs (338A) and Backward Classes (338B); Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities (350B)
subsections: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities and Art. 350A
AP State Commission for SCs and STs

accepted.s:
Which one of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Body — Article

1. National Commission for Scheduled Castes — Article 338
2. National Commission for Scheduled Tribes — Article 338A
3. National Commission for Backward Classes — Article 338B
accepted.x: The NCSC, NCST and NCBC are provided for under Articles 338, 338A and 338B respectively.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure Article–body pairs and eliminate codes containing a swapped constitutional provision.

accepted.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, as a combined commission, was created by the
accepted.x: The 65th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1990 created the combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes under Article 338.
accepted.tq: Use the amendment-number trap by distinguishing the original provision from the later bifurcation.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The 65th Constitutional Amendment replaced the original Special Officer for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
2. The 65th Constitutional Amendment also replaced the commission established by the 1987 Resolution.
3. The 65th Constitutional Amendment created the separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes under Article 338A.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Separate constitutional provision for the NCST under Article 338A came through the 89th Amendment, not the 65th Amendment.
accepted.tq: Check the amendment sequence carefully; the false statement swaps the combined commission with the later bifurcation.

accepted.s: The bifurcation of the combined National Commission for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes into separate NCSC and NCST was effected by the
accepted.x: The 89th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003 bifurcated the combined commission, creating separate constitutional commissions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.
accepted.tq: Discriminate between closely related amendment numbers by matching the amendment with its precise institutional change.

accepted.s: The National Commission for Scheduled Tribes was set up on
accepted.x: The NCST was set up on 19 February 2004 pursuant to the 89th Constitutional Amendment, 2003.
accepted.tq: Treat the exact establishment date as distinct from the year of the constitutional amendment.

accepted.s: Which of the following correctly describes the constitutional position of the National Commission for Backward Classes before the 102nd Constitutional Amendment?
o: It was a constitutional body under Article 338B from 1993.
It was a body created by the 89th Constitutional Amendment.
It was a statutory body under the NCBC Act, 1993.
It was a constitutional body under Article 350B.
accepted.x: Before receiving constitutional status through the 102nd Amendment, the NCBC functioned as a statutory body under the NCBC Act, 1993.
accepted.tq: Separate statutory status before an amendment from constitutional status after the amendment.

accepted.s: The separate Ministry of Tribal Affairs, established in 1999, was significant because it
o: created the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities
paved the way for a separate National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
abolished the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes
transferred Article 338A to the State List
accepted.x: The establishment of the separate Ministry of Tribal Affairs in 1999 paved the way for the creation of a separate NCST.
accepted.tq: Link the institutional cause with its stated administrative consequence rather than confusing it with formal constitutional creation.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a function of the National Commissions for the protected communities?
o: Inquiring into specific complaints of deprivation of rights
Investigating and monitoring constitutional and legal safeguards
Adjudicating criminal cases and awarding punishment to offenders
Advising on socio-economic planning and evaluating progress
accepted.x: The Commissions investigate safeguards, inquire into complaints and advise on development; they do not function as criminal courts or award criminal punishment.
accepted.tq: Find the institutionally impossible power by asking which function belongs to a court rather than a commission.

accepted.s: In respect of reports of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes, which one of the following is correct?
o: The Commission submits its reports directly to the Supreme Court for approval.
The Commission submits its reports annually to the Prime Minister, who lays them before Parliament.
The Commission submits its reports to the President, who lays them before Parliament with a memorandum of action taken.
The Commission submits its reports only to the concerned State Governor.
accepted.x: The Commission submits annual or other appropriate reports to the President. The President lays them before Parliament along with a memorandum of action taken; State-related reports are sent to the Governor.
accepted.tq: Use the authority trap: distinguish the President, who receives and lays the report, from the Prime Minister or Governor.

accepted.s:
With reference to the reports of the National Commissions, consider the following statements:
1. A report may be submitted annually or whenever the Commission considers it necessary.
2. Reports relating to State matters are sent to the Governor.
3. The President lays the reports before Parliament with a memorandum of action taken.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The reporting arrangement includes annual or need-based reports, transmission of State-related reports to the Governor and laying before Parliament with an action-taken memorandum.
accepted.tq: Test the full reporting chain rather than focusing only on the authority to whom the report is submitted.

accepted.s:
While investigating a matter, the National Commission may exercise the powers of a civil court in respect of which of the following?
1. Summoning and examining a person on oath
2. Requiring the discovery and production of documents
3. Receiving evidence on affidavits
4. Requisitioning public records from a court or office
5. Issuing commissions for the examination of witnesses
Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: All the listed powers are available to the Commission while inquiring into matters, including summoning persons, requiring documents, receiving affidavit evidence, requisitioning records and issuing witness commissions.
accepted.tq: When several procedural powers are listed, verify whether the entire set belongs to the civil-court power rather than excluding the final item.

accepted.s: The Union Government and every State Government are required to consult the Commission on
o: only matters relating to elections to local bodies
all major policy matters affecting the concerned protected community
every item of financial legislation before introduction
all appointments to the higher judiciary
accepted.x: Article 338(9) and Article 338A(9) require consultation with the concerned Commission on all major policy matters affecting Scheduled Castes or Scheduled Tribes, as applicable.
accepted.tq: Avoid the scope trap: the consultation requirement concerns major policy matters affecting the community, not every governmental decision.

accepted.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Castes constituted separately in 2004?
accepted.x: Suraj Bhan was the first Chairperson of the separately constituted National Commission for Scheduled Castes in 2004.
accepted.tq: Discriminate among chairpersons by linking each name to the correct commission and period.

accepted.s: Who was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes constituted separately in 2004?
accepted.x: Kunwar Singh was the first Chairperson of the National Commission for Scheduled Tribes constituted separately in 2004.
accepted.tq: Use the commission–chairperson association instead of relying only on the common year of constitution.

accepted.s: The first Chairperson of the constitutionally established National Commission for Backward Classes in 2019 was
accepted.x: Bhagwan Lal Sahni was the first Chairperson of the constitutionally established NCBC in 2019.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the first chairperson of the constitutional NCBC from chairpersons of other commissions.

accepted.s: Who was serving as Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes in the current reference period?
accepted.x: Niranjan Jyoti is identified as the current Chairperson of the National Commission for Backward Classes in the stated reference period.
accepted.tq: Separate a current office-holder from the first office-holder of the same commission.

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements regarding the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is correct?
o: The officer is appointed by the President and reports to the President.
The officer is appointed by the Chief Minister and reports to the Governor.
The officer is appointed by the Parliament and reports to the Prime Minister.
The officer is appointed by the Governor and reports to the State Legislature.
accepted.x: Under Article 350B, the Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities is appointed by the President and submits reports to the President.
accepted.tq: Apply the authority trap by matching appointment and reporting powers with the President.
accepted.sec: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities and Art. 350A

accepted.s: The headquarters of the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities is located at
accepted.x: The office styled as the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities has its headquarters at Prayagraj, formerly Allahabad.
accepted.tq: Test the exact headquarters rather than the more obvious national-capital location.
accepted.sec: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities and Art. 350A

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. Articles 350A and 350B were inserted by the 7th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1956.
2. The amendment was associated with the reorganisation of States.
3. The office under Article 350B is styled as the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. The 7th Amendment of 1956, connected with the States Reorganisation process, inserted Articles 350A and 350B and provided for the Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities.
accepted.tq: Combine amendment, context and official designation; all three details refer to the same constitutional arrangement.
accepted.sec: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities and Art. 350A

accepted.s:
Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?

Article — Subject

a. Article 347 — Recognition of a language spoken by a substantial section of a State
b. Article 350 — Representation for the redress of grievances in any language used in the Union or a State
c. Article 350A — Mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage

Select the correct answer using the code given below.
accepted.x: Article 347 concerns recognition of a language spoken by a substantial section of a State; Article 350 concerns representation in any language used in the Union or a State; and Article 350A concerns mother-tongue instruction at the primary stage.
accepted.tq: Use the article-number sequence to distinguish the closely related linguistic safeguards.
accepted.sec: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities and Art. 350A

accepted.s: Which one of the following statements about linguistic minorities is correct?
o: They are notified under the National Commission for Minorities Act, and Article 350B has no role concerning them.
They are covered exclusively by Article 338B.
They are treated only as religious minorities for purposes of constitutional safeguards.
They are not notified under the National Commission for Minorities Act and are covered by the officer under Article 350B.
accepted.x: Linguistic minorities are not notified under the National Commission for Minorities Act; safeguards for them are covered through the officer provided under Article 350B.
accepted.tq: Separate linguistic-minority coverage under Article 350B from the statutory framework of the National Commission for Minorities.
accepted.sec: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities and Art. 350A

accepted.s: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities launched a programme consisting of
o: a twelve-point programme for tribal development
a ten-point programme to preserve language and culture
a five-point programme to promote official-language use
a seven-point programme for State reorganisation
accepted.x: The Commissioner for Linguistic Minorities launched a 10-point programme aimed at preserving the language and culture of linguistic minorities.
accepted.tq: Treat the numerical feature as decisive and avoid substituting the nearby States Reorganisation or tribal-development figures.
accepted.sec: Special Officer for Linguistic Minorities and Art. 350A

accepted.s: Which statement correctly describes the constitutional basis of State Commissions for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes?
o: State Commissions are created by the Supreme Court under Article 32.
State Commissions are created only by the President through an executive order under Article 350B.
State Commissions are created by State law; Articles 338(9) and 338A(9) concern consultation on major policy matters.
Every State Commission is automatically created directly by Article 338(9).
accepted.x: State Commissions are created through State legislation. Articles 338(9) and 338A(9) deal with consultation on major policy matters and do not empower the President to create State Commissions.
accepted.tq: Reject the wrong-authority trap by distinguishing a State legislative creation from a constitutional consultation clause.
accepted.sec: AP State Commission for SCs and STs

accepted.s: Which one of the following persons was identified as the Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Castes during the review of welfare schemes in SPSR Nellore?
accepted.x: K.S. Jawahar was identified as the Chairman of the Andhra Pradesh State Commission for Scheduled Castes while reviewing SC/ST welfare schemes in SPSR Nellore.
accepted.tq: Keep State-level office-holders separate from chairpersons of the corresponding national commissions.
accepted.sec: AP State Commission for SCs and STs
